boards.name: 5 Whys
boards.description: Trace a problem back to its root cause by asking “why?” five times, then agree a fix that addresses the cause, not the symptom.

cards.title: 5 Whys — the newsletter went out with broken links
cards.body: A blameless look at one incident. Ask why until the answer is something we can change in the process.

cards.title: How to use this template
cards.body: Write the problem as a fact. Each “why” answers the card before it. Stop when you reach a process cause (not a person). The fix goes against the root cause.

cards.title: Problem
cards.body: Tuesday’s newsletter went to 12,000 people with three broken links.

cards.title: Why 1
cards.body: The links pointed to pages that had been renamed.

cards.title: Why 2
cards.body: The website was restructured on Monday; nobody told the newsletter team.

cards.title: Why 3
cards.body: Website changes aren’t announced outside the web team.

cards.title: Why 4
cards.body: There is no shared release calendar for content.

cards.title: Why 5 — root cause
cards.body: Teams plan content separately, with no step that checks links before sending.

cards.title: Fixes
cards.body:
- Shared content calendar (owner: comms lead)
- Redirects added automatically when a page is renamed
- Link check step in the newsletter checklist
